evidence: Only '3.14' and '12:34' had row content asserted, so 21+ glyphs including the 4-cell ')' were checked for width only; the agent added a Python-baselined digits_charset fixture and a test that reads the committed .txt, which is one of the reviewer's offered remedies, and mutation-checked it by corrupting '5'.
guidance_note: When a file's own comment names mistranscription as the likeliest defect, ship a baseline-derived assertion over the whole table in the original PR rather than a width-only check.

evidence: 9e0523f's new digits_charset.py docstring says 'the second 36', but GLYPHS gives ')' four cells so 'ABCDEF $£€()' is 11x3+4 = 37; the agent admits it took 36 from get_width, the function that miscounts ')'.
guidance_note: When a fix writes a derived number into a comment, compute it from the rendered baseline the fix just generated (the .txt row length), not from the upstream width function the fixture exists to disprove.

evidence: Duplicate of F2 on the same docstring line from 9e0523f: 36 vs the actual 37 rendered cells; fixed in the same commit e9042fd.
guidance_note: When a fix writes a derived number into a comment, compute it from the rendered baseline the fix just generated, not from the upstream width function the fixture exists to disprove.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: glyphFor's [' ', ' ', drawn] fallback and its 'occupy a single cell' comment are original round-0 code that 9e0523f did not touch. The misalignment is real but the agent showed upstream renders Digits('文1') with the same misalignment, so a placeholder would diverge from the oracle; it declined the code change, fixed the false comment, and pinned the behaviour with a test.
guidance_note: Never state a width or size property in a port's doc comment ('occupies a single cell') without checking it against a wide-character input first.

evidence: A '\n' in value reaches rows[2] and digitsContent's join yields four lines, falsifying the readonly [string,string,string] three-row type; the agent confirmed upstream also emits four lines, then fixed it narrowly by adding '\n' and '\r' to REPLACEMENTS and declined the tab half, since a tab keeps three rows.
guidance_note: When a type promises a shape (three single-line rows), sweep every path a raw input character reaches that shape for line terminators in the original PR.

evidence: 9e0523f's comments say 21 new characters, but basic/large draw only 1,2,3,4,: from GLYPHS ('.' is not a key), so 27-5=22; the agent deleted the count from both files instead of changing it, so it cannot drift again.
guidance_note: Leave derived counts out of comments the fix writes; 'the characters no other fixture draws' says the same and cannot go stale.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the test 'gives every character the font knows exactly three cells' with loop string '0123456789+-^x:ABCDEF$£€ ' is visible as unchanged context in 9e0523f, so it predates review and e9042fd did not touch it. It omits '(' and ')' although ')' is 4 cells; the agent deleted it as a weaker duplicate of the baseline-derived charset test.
guidance_note: When a test title says 'every X', check that the loop's domain is literally every X and does not quietly drop the exception the PR documents.

narrative: The F1 fix (a Python-baselined charset fixture plus a derived test) was sound and mutation-checked, but it left two miscounted numbers in new comments (36 vs 37 cells, 21 vs 22 characters), which became three round-1 findings. Round 1 would have run anyway because F4 and F5 hit original glyphFor code, and F7 in round 2 also hit original code. The agent checked upstream before every pushback and documented the newline divergence on purpose.
guidance_observations: Each derived number the fix wrote into a comment came back as a finding; computing numbers from the generated baseline, or leaving them out, would have removed three threads.
The agent proactively fixed a neighbouring overclaiming test title in the F7 round, which is the right sweep habit applied one round late.

evidence: With index === start and no lastSpace, the hard-break arm returns [index, index], so paragraphOffsets never advances; the agent reproduced heap exhaustion on Content('文').wrap(1) and fixed the arm to consume one character.
guidance_note: For any loop driven by a 'next offset' helper, write a forward-progress test with an input wider than the budget before shipping.

evidence: contentOf(size) received the outer measured size while renderVisual cropped to the inner width; the agent confirmed upstream Widget.size is the content area (40x7 with padding/border reports 34x3), added resolveVisualRenderHeight, and passed the content area to contentOf.
guidance_note: When a callback is handed a size, decide and test in the original PR whether that size is the outer region or the content area, using a bordered and padded case.

evidence: Same zero-progress defect as F1: Content('文').wrap(1) spins; fixed in 2303912 with index + character.length progress and tested at width 1.
guidance_note: For any loop driven by a 'next offset' helper, write a forward-progress test with an input wider than the budget before shipping.

evidence: At width 5, 'hello  world' left the second space as leading content; Rich and Textual both give ['hello','world'] there. The skipSpaces fix in 2303912 fixed width 5 but kept 'space = index' when the overflowing character is a space, which F9 then found. The agent verified against Rich, not Textual, which the PR's later issue comment admits was the wrong oracle.
guidance_note: Verify wrap semantics against Textual itself (the port's oracle) across a family of widths for one input, not at the single width the reviewer quoted.

evidence: Third report of the F1 zero-progress loop; covered by the same 2303912 fix and its width-1 tests.
guidance_note: For any loop driven by a 'next offset' helper, write a forward-progress test with an input wider than the budget before shipping.

evidence: The test titled 'wraps back to the first colour' only asserted toHaveLength(12), which passes with the modulo deleted; 2303912 adds placeholderColorClass(12)===(0), (13)===(1) and (5)!==(0), and the agent confirmed deleting the modulo now fails.
guidance_note: Before committing a test, delete the line its title names and confirm the test fails.

evidence: The F2 fix's new test 'fills a bordered, padded box edge to edge' claims the no-holes guarantee survives styling but asserts only on stripAnsi output; the agent's raw frame showed the padding columns carry no SGR. It took the reviewer's 'acknowledge' option, narrowed the test name and comment, added a background-SGR assertion, and filed the hole separately.
guidance_note: A test that claims anything about colour or background must assert on the raw frame; stripAnsi cannot tell a painted cell from a hole.

evidence: 2303912 added resolveVisualRenderHeight to src/content/index.ts only, while its sibling resolveVisualRenderWidth is also in the top-level src/index.ts; f127afa adds it there.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a sibling of an existing public function, grep every barrel that exports the original and add the sibling to each.

evidence: The reviewer said 'hello  world' at width 6 should be ['hello','world']. The agent rejected that expected value using Rich ('hello ') and made the code keep trailing spaces that fit. The PR's own issue comment later shows Textual gives ['hello','world'] at widths 6 and 7, so the reviewer was right for the port's oracle and the agent's change moved widths 7 and 8 further from Textual, which needed another fix in 5f47ea8.
guidance_note: Before pushing back on an expected value in a port, run the case against the upstream being ported (Textual's Content.wrap), not a related library (Rich).

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the code-point walk (String.fromCodePoint(paragraph.codePointAt(index))) is in the round-0 nextLineBreak, and 2303912 left it alone. The agent showed per-code-point cellLen measures the family emoji as 8 and splits it at width 4, then fixed it with Intl.Segmenter grapheme clusters.
guidance_note: When rewriting a text-measuring loop, walk grapheme clusters from the start and test with a ZWJ emoji at a narrow width.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the useState initializer calling nextPlaceholderColorIndex is round-0 code that 2303912 did not touch. The impurity is real; the agent made the claim idempotent with a ref (??=) instead of the suggested effect, to avoid an unpainted first frame. The new test drives a click re-render, not a StrictMode double-invoke, so the packet does not show the StrictMode case was exercised.
guidance_note: Any render-time call that mutates shared state gets a re-render test in the original PR that asserts the state advanced exactly once.

evidence: The reviewer hedged that an empty <Text> might take a row at zero content height; the agent rendered height: 2; border: round and got exactly two rows ('╭╮','╰╯'), and pointed out that only the width axis has renderVisual's one-column floor. The finding targets the height axis the F2 fix introduced.

The flag is a false positive: the unmemoised visualize(contentOf(...)) and its 'not work worth memoising' comment are round-0 code that 2303912 only reshaped. A string goes through Content.fromMarkup, so the comment was false; f127afa restores memoisation in a ContentBody component.
guidance_note: When removing a useMemo, check what each arm of the memoised function actually costs before writing a comment that says it is cheap.

evidence: f127afa's useMemo keys on [content, width, height], so a resize re-parses markup for value content that cannot depend on size. The reviewer's variable-length deps array would trigger React's deps-size warning; the agent instead split resolution so values are visualised outside the measured pass and functions inside it.
guidance_note: When adding a memo over a union input, key each arm only on what that arm actually reads, splitting at the union's discriminator.

evidence: The claim-before-parse order is in the round-0 code too (useState claim, then parsePlaceholderVariant), so the F11 ref rewrite inherited it rather than causing it. The reviewer admits it is inert today because the whole render fails; the agent still reordered cheaply and pinned it with a two-root shared-app test.
guidance_note: Order render bodies as parse inputs first, then perform shared side effects, so a throw never leaves a spent claim behind.

evidence: The F8 fix added only resolveVisualRenderHeight to src/index.ts while the six align exports in src/content/index.ts were still missing from it; the agent itself notes 'this same gap has now been found twice a round apart' and added all six plus a root-export test.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds one export missing from a barrel, diff the whole sub-barrel against the root barrel and close every gap in the same commit.

evidence: The reviewer's hypothesis was conditional on truncate leaving an over-wide glyph whole; the agent showed new Content('文').truncate(1).plain is '' (cellLength 0), so padRow fills to box.width, and it added the requested invariant test anyway. It is about the over-wide line the F1 hard-break fix can now produce.
Duplicate of F16 (align exports absent from src/index.ts), fixed once in 64cb7eb.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds one export missing from a barrel, diff the whole sub-barrel against the root barrel and close every gap in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: ContentSource was introduced and retyped onto public props in the round-0 code; f127afa only added comments and imports around it. A consumer could no longer name the type of a public prop, so exporting it was right.
guidance_note: When a PR retypes a public prop, export the new type from every barrel that exports the props interface.

narrative: A wrap rewrite and a content-area seam drew 19 findings over three request-changes rounds. Rounds 1 and 2 would have run anyway because each had findings on original code (F10, F11, F13, F19), but more than half of their findings came from fix commits: barrel exports added one at a time, a test overclaiming its coverage, and a memo keyed too broadly. The costliest chain was F4 to F9: the agent verified whitespace semantics against Rich rather than Textual, rejected the reviewer's correct expected value, and only discovered and reverted the error in a post-review issue comment.
guidance_observations: Choosing the wrong oracle (Rich instead of Textual) turned a correct reviewer finding into a pushback and an extra fix cycle; a port should verify against the upstream it ports, and nothing else.
Public-surface gaps came back twice a round apart; sweeping the sub-barrel against the root barrel at the first report would have closed F16/F18 in round 1.
Mutation-checking each fix was consistent and caught tests that would have passed vacuously (F6, F11, F15).

evidence: The agent confirmed uv.lock is gitignored at .gitignore:16 and pyproject asks only textual>=1.0.0, so 'pinned reference' was false; it took the reviewer's 'soften to verified against' option, added a version-check command, and filed the pin decision as a ticket.
guidance_note: Before writing 'pinned' or any reproducibility claim in a doc, check with git ls-files that the file the claim rests on is tracked.

evidence: button.ts:21,35 and toggle.ts:23,40 use Content.fromText on purpose, and button_markup asserts markup renders, so the blanket 'labels use new Content' rule was dangerous; the agent took the reviewer's second option and stated the discriminator (opaque text vs markup-accepting prop).
guidance_note: When generalising one widget's fix into a doc rule, grep the other call sites of both alternatives before stating it as universal.

evidence: render_pngs.ts:72 runs render-fixture-xvfb.sh inside docker for every JS target, so 'which run.sh never calls' was false; the rewrite keeps only the true claim, that Gate 4 never invokes uv.
guidance_note: Before writing 'never calls' about a script, trace the call graph transitively, not just the top-level file.

narrative: A CLAUDE.md rewrite drew three factual-accuracy findings, all correct, all fixed by verifying against the repo in one fix commit. The reviewer approved the next round. No finding came from a fix.
guidance_observations: All three errors were unverified claims in a document whose stated premise is that every claim was checked; running git ls-files and grep on each assertion before committing would have cleared round 0.

evidence: AUTO = 'auto' at box-geometry.ts:11 was module-private while button-component.tsx re-typed the literal; the agent exported AUTO and imported it, and chose that over a new predicate wrapper.
guidance_note: Before typing a sentinel literal, grep for an existing constant and export it rather than restating it.

evidence: contentWidth = (explicitWidth ?? minWidth) || ... truncated a -full-width label to 14 while renderRows painted at measured.width = 80; the agent moved truncation inside renderRows(width) so both read one width, and showed the old formula fails two new tests.
guidance_note: When changing how a widget computes its paint width, grep every other derivation of 'how wide am I' in the same component and route them all through the one value.

evidence: visual-tests/README.md:106 showed 'Summary: 1 match, 2 diff, 0 skipped', which lacked the new known-diff field and used a field name compare.ts never printed; the README now shows the real four-field format.
guidance_note: When changing a CLI's printed output format, grep the docs for the old output string in the same commit.

evidence: makeScalarSpec does return normalize: makeScalarNormalize(axis), and the string comes from scalar.ts's Unit.PERCENT toInk; the agent corrected both copies. The law token was cited for the shorter replacement text, but what decided the fix was correctness, not subtraction.
guidance_note: Before naming a mechanism in a comment or doc, open the cited function and confirm it does what the sentence says.

narrative: Four round-0 findings, all correct, all fixed in two commits: a duplicated sentinel, a truncation width left on the old formula after the paint width changed, a stale README example, and a false mechanism claim in CLAUDE.md and a code comment. The reviewer approved the next round. No finding came from a fix.
guidance_observations: F2 and F4 both came from the agent's own explanatory text and its half-applied single-source refactor; the PR's comment claimed one-source-of-truth while leaving a second width derivation in place.

evidence: At widths 0-2, innerWidth went negative and each row still painted 3 cells, wider than the declared box. Instead of the suggested geometry floor, the agent clamped innerWidth at 0 and cropped each row to width, which it says matches Textual's border-box crop; it mutation-checked a 0-4 width sweep.
guidance_note: For any geometry function, test the degenerate widths (0 to the fixed-chrome width) and assert that the output fits the box in the original PR.

evidence: stackTop clamped the position to 0 and let the stack render past the viewport; the agent read upstream's ToastRack overflow-y: scroll plus scroll_end and replaced it with fitStack, which clips oldest rows off the top. That is the reviewer's 'truncate to fit' option. But the fix had its own off-by-one (F4), and its test encoded that bug as top: 0.
guidance_note: When a fix models upstream scroll behaviour, write the expected positions from the upstream model (last N rows of the full stack) rather than reading them back from the new function's output.

evidence: An out-of-union severity from compiled-JS callers produced '--undefined' and an error blaming the theme. That misattribution was real, but defaulting to 'information' would silently miscolour. The agent parsed severity at the single new Notification call site, threw naming the bad value, and derived the union from the runtime list.
guidance_note: Parse every string-union field at the constructor that admits it from outside, so downstream lookup tables are total by construction.

evidence: fitStack, added in 21567b8 for F2, charged a gap for a toast that renders zero rows, so fitStack(blocksOf(3,4),11) returned top 0 and left the stack one row above the floor. The agent's hand trace (14 rows, show the last 10) confirmed top should be 1. The F2 fix's own test asserted top: 0, encoding the bug.
guidance_note: When writing a budget-spending loop, charge each item's overhead only after deciding the item is shown, and add an invariant test that top + painted + gaps equals the budget.

narrative: Round 0 found two real edge cases in toast geometry and stacking, both fixed by modelling upstream behaviour. The F2 fix's new fitStack had an off-by-one gap charge, and its own test pinned the wrong top value; the reviewer caught it in round 1. Round 1 would still have run because F3 (unvalidated severity) was on original code.
guidance_observations: The F2 fix shipped with an example test whose expected value was read from the implementation; the invariant test added in the F4 fix (top + painted + gaps === rack) would have caught it in the first fix.
The agent consistently derived the degradation shape from upstream source before choosing a fix, which avoided invented floors and defaults.
